why: A's proposition_8_1_16 concludes TX.IsZhou from X.IsZhou only under the extra hypothesis X.TangentZhouReflect: for a smooth b ∈ TX and (g, h) ∈ G_b, T(g, h) = id on T_b(TX) implies Tg = id on T_{p(b)}X. This is the step of the text's proof that differentiates (8.16) and uses that Tτ_X is onto; B (the text's statement) has no such hypothesis, and nothing in B's premise X.IsZhou gives it. It is satisfiable (tangentZhouReflect_trivial) and believed always true, but proving it needs second-tangent calculus (Tτ_X : T(TX) → TX onto, chain rule for T(Ts), T(Tt)) that the project does not formalize, so A ⇒ B fails for effort only. B ⇒ A: proposition_8_1_16 is B with the hypothesis dropped, the point example is B at pointEpGroupoid; the other four conjuncts (levelVal_tangentProj_mem_smoothSet, mem_nonEffectivePart_tangent, tangentMor_trivial, tangentZhouReflect_trivial) are lemmas/witnesses not implied by B and were re-proved outright. Universes at 0 (TX lives in Type 1).
